title: 10 CFR Part 21 — Reporting of Defects and Noncompliance
versionMode: Live source link + client-controlled interpretation overlay

sources.label: NRC guidance on implementing 10 CFR Part 21
RG 1.234 — Evaluating Deviations and Reporting Defects and Noncompliance
NEI 14-09 — Guidelines for Implementation of 10 CFR Part 21

sections.title: Purpose
sections.summary: Establishes procedures and requirements for implementing the Energy Reorganization Act provisions addressed by Part 21.
obligations: Maintain a process that can identify and evaluate reportable defects and noncompliance.
sections.ifUnmet: The organization may not have a controlled basis for deciding when a condition enters Part 21 evaluation.

sections.title: Scope
sections.summary: Defines the entities, facilities, activities, and basic components within the scope of Part 21.
obligations: Determine whether the organization, activity, basic component, or supplier is subject to Part 21.
sections.ifUnmet: A condition could be evaluated under the wrong regulatory pathway or not evaluated at all.

sections.title: Definitions
sections.summary: Provides the defined terms used by Part 21, including basic component, defect, deviation, failure to comply, and substantial safety hazard.
obligations: Use controlled definitions when classifying a deviation, defect, or failure to comply.
sections.ifUnmet: The system may produce an inconsistent or unsupported classification.

sections.title: Interpretations
sections.summary: Provides the Commission interpretation pathway for Part 21 requirements and makes interpretation governance an explicit control point.
obligations: Record the client-approved interpretation used for a compliance conclusion.
sections.ifUnmet: An agent may apply an unapproved interpretation to a regulatory conclusion.

sections.title: Communications
sections.summary: Defines communication expectations relevant to Part 21 information and responsible contacts.
obligations: Maintain controlled communications and access to responsible contacts.
sections.ifUnmet: Affected personnel may not know how to escalate a potentially reportable condition.

sections.title: Posting requirements
sections.summary: Sets notice and posting expectations for Part 21 information and contacts.
obligations: Maintain required postings and access to the responsible contacts.
sections.ifUnmet: Affected personnel may not know how to escalate a potentially reportable condition.

sections.title: Exemptions
sections.summary: Provides the Commission's exemption authority and identifies boundaries that require careful applicability analysis.
obligations: Record the legal basis for any claimed exemption or exclusion.
sections.ifUnmet: A false exemption assumption can mask a reportability obligation.

sections.title: Information collection requirements: OMB approval
sections.summary: Identifies the approved information collection requirements associated with Part 21.
obligations: Maintain the controlled forms and records needed for the approved information collection requirements.
sections.ifUnmet: The audit record may omit required information or use an uncontrolled collection mechanism.

sections.title: Notification of failure to comply or existence of a defect and its evaluation
sections.summary: Requires procedures to evaluate deviations and failures to comply for defects or failures associated with substantial safety hazards, including escalation and notification paths.
obligations: Evaluate deviations and failures to comply as soon as practicable and within the applicable time window.
Escalate qualifying results to the responsible officer or designated person.
Preserve the evaluation and notification decision basis.
sections.ifUnmet: A potentially reportable defect may not be evaluated, escalated, or notified within the required window.

sections.title: Procurement documents
sections.summary: Sets procurement-document expectations relevant to Part 21 responsibilities and supplied basic components.
obligations: Flow down applicable Part 21 responsibilities and acceptance requirements into procurement documents.
sections.ifUnmet: Supplier responsibilities and evidence expectations may not be contractually controlled.

sections.title: Inspections
sections.summary: Provides the inspection context for activities and records governed by Part 21.
obligations: Make relevant records and responsible personnel available for inspection.
sections.ifUnmet: The organization may not be able to demonstrate control of the evidence during inspection.

sections.title: Maintenance and inspection of records
sections.summary: Requires records supporting Part 21 evaluations and the ability to make them available for inspection.
obligations: Maintain complete, legible, retrievable, and auditable Part 21 records.
Preserve records that support both reportable and non-reportable evaluation decisions.
sections.ifUnmet: The conclusion may be impossible to defend because the evidence chain and decision history are incomplete.

sections.title: Failure to notify
sections.summary: Addresses failure-to-notify consequences and reinforces the need for a controlled, accountable notification decision path.
obligations: Escalate a potentially reportable condition through the approved notification workflow.
Preserve the basis for the notification or non-notification decision.
sections.ifUnmet: A required notification may be late, incomplete, or unsupported.

sections.title: Criminal penalties
sections.summary: Identifies criminal penalty implications associated with violations of Part 21.
obligations: Escalate suspected deliberate or material violations through approved legal and compliance channels.
sections.ifUnmet: The organization may mishandle a potentially serious violation or fail to preserve the required decision path.

implementationGuidance.title: Evaluate deviations and report defects using an accepted method
steps: Evaluate the deviation or failure to comply
Determine defect / substantial safety hazard significance
